description: Take a freshly created project from idea to a validated blueprint by default; feature implementation and build validation require an explicit opt-in.
name: new-app-from-idea

parameters.description: Stop after the validated blueprint; set to false to implement features
parameters.name: stopBeforeImplementation

configJson.prompt: Validate the blueprint only. Confirm roadmap.json includes an MVP milestone; every MVP feature is backlog; every post-MVP feature is waiting_approval; all features have passes:false; and the aidd metadata gates pass. Every product feature must also map to a valid roadmap milestone, and MVP must be the first incomplete milestone, or readiness stays blocked. Run bun run smoke:qc. Fix blueprint/scaffold defects only and implement no product features. Commit every non-ignored scaffold or blueprint path with a clear initialization commit; when .aidd artifacts are ignored, keep them as validated local state and never force-add them. If every deliverable is ignored metadata, do not create an empty commit. Optionally record the first dependency-ready MVP feature and its future `bun run start -- --project-dir {projectDir} --feature <id>` command in .aidd/next-implementation.md, but do not run it.

Write a first-session report to .aidd/reports/first-session.md (overwrite if present; record the current date inside it). Read the per-step timing and outcome data from {sessionMetricsPath}, which the pipeline wrote for this session and refreshed after every completed step, and summarize: manual interventions that were needed, assumptions that turned out wrong, per-step elapsed time, and the final build/validation gate result — when stopBeforeImplementation left the implementation and validation steps skipped, say so and report the blueprint step's smoke:qc as the last gate. Then list the generated feature backlog counts (implemented vs backlog) and the recommended next actions to reach a shippable v1. Write nothing outside .aidd/.
